acceptedAs.reason: pass -> fail. Fits GATE-A1 (FALSE PASS): the old test equalled its reference only because both lost their page size. Chrome prints test AND reference at 540 x 432 pt (7.5in x 6in, the tentative @page width/height descriptors). Old vellora printed both at 360 x 216 pt (the 5in x 3in UA box): its @page reader did not strip the CSS comment in front of the test's `size: 1234px`, so it read the property name '/* ... */ size' and dropped the declaration; the reference has no size. Now comments are stripped and the test gets `size: 1234px` (925.5 x 925.5 pt, CSS Paged Media 3), the reference keeps 360 x 216; vellora does not implement the tentative width/height descriptors (follow-up).

position-mm.label: DESIGN TARGET
position-mm.why: word/anchor position error vs a reference (REF-W max/p95, REF-R worst anchor, DANFE-L1, LET-1). 0.1 mm (0.28 pt, 0.38 CSS px) is 10x the 0.01 mm the values are reported with and below one CSS px (0.26 mm), the smallest step a px-snapping layout can move; the measurement is deterministic for one build and one reference (CONFIRMED: equal inputs gave equal values in the Phase A repeat run).

geometry-excess-mm.label: DESIGN TARGET
geometry-excess-mm.why: distance OUTSIDE a specification window (BOL-G*, DANFE-B*, DANFE-M1, TXT-A1). Inside the window the spec admits any value, so only the excess is ratcheted; 0.05 mm is about one 600 dpi raster pixel (0.042 mm), the measurement quantum of measure_bars.py / the page ink box.

font-excess-pt.label: SPEC-derived tolerance unit
font-excess-pt.why: font-size excess outside a window; 0.05 pt is the tolerance ACCEPTANCE.md already applies to every font-size criterion (BOL-T*, DANFE-F*).

count.label: DESIGN TARGET
count.why: integer counts from deterministic tools (required strings found, extractor missing/extra tokens, segments/glyphs attributed, decoded symbols): any loss is a real change of the document.

page-delta.label: DESIGN TARGET
page-delta.why: |vellora pages - reference pages|: a page break moving is never noise.

pdf-probe-pt.label: DESIGN TARGET
pdf-probe-pt.why: per-word |dx| / |dy| of vellora's PDF vs Chrome's PDF (pdftotext -bbox, same-page pairs). 1 pt (0.35 mm) is an order of magnitude below the Phase A regressions it must catch (invoice price column +9 pt, notification signature -14 pt) and above glyph-bbox rounding of pdftotext (0.01 pt) and sub-px snapping differences.
